$comment: The mutation floor and the complexity cap, per declared scope.
Specs: docs/spec/the-ratchet.md, and docs/spec/complexity-on-the-trend-layer.md §4.
This file is beside stryker.config.mjs on purpose: `configHash` below ties the two
together, and a diff that changes the timeout and re-derives the floors should show
both changes in the same directory.
EVERY FLOOR AND EVERY CAP IS `unarmed`, AND NOTHING HERE REFUSES ANYTHING YET. Both
are derived from observed history and applied ONCE, BY HAND, at arming. Arming is a
human judgement, per scope, after that scope's window fills. There is no moment at
which `the ratchet` becomes armed; every entry is its own decision. `pnpm deploy:site`
prints how far each window has filled at every deploy.
The rule initialises; it does not maintain.
A floor is the LOWEST score a scope reached across consecutive healthy CI runs covering
TEN DISTINCT TREES, with no gap over 3 days. After arming it moves UP by hand and never
down on its own
— re-deriving is lowering, and costs a justification like any other lowering.
`floor`   a number this scope may not score under, or `unarmed`.
`armed`   the date the entry was added, or the date it was armed. It is what makes
`unarmed for 94 days` printable, and it is the only guard on somebody
typing `unarmed` to make a refusal go away.
`ignored` disable directives in this scope's mutated source. Asserted against a real
sweep of the tree by `gates/ignored-mutants.test.ts`, at merge. There are
zero in this repo, so any increase is a real event.
`notes`   APPEND-ONLY, one line per lowering, never cleared. A bare number going 44.1
to 41.0 is a diff that says nothing about why; the justification belongs
next to the permission, permanently, where whoever next opens this file
reads it. Nothing enforces this — the file makes an omission visible, it
does not make it impossible.
THE RATCHET, MIRRORED, because for these two series the bad direction is UP. A cap is
the HIGHEST value a scope reached across its calibration window, applied once, at
arming. After arming it moves DOWN only, by hand. RAISING A CAP IS THE LOWERING OF
THIS FILE and costs a `notes` entry exactly like one.
`caps`    per series, and only `complexity-max` and `complexity-mass-over-10` may
appear. `complexity-functions` and `complexity-mass` are NOT capped, by
decision: they grow with the codebase legitimately, and a cap on either
would refuse a feature. Naming one of them here is a parse error, not a
silently ignored key — a typo must not read as protection.
`cap`     a number this scope may not exceed for that series, or `unarmed`.
`armed`   as above, and it guards the same temptation.
`notes`   APPEND-ONLY, one line per raising.
THE CAP WINDOW IS THE FLOOR'S WINDOW: CI nightlies only, consecutive healthy runs covering
TEN DISTINCT TREES, no gap over 3 days, counted in TREES — not runs and not days. Both are
walked by one `streakOf` in scripts/lib/floors.ts, so the two cannot drift apart. A full
window may hold MORE THAN TEN ROWS: a row repeating a tree already inside it is kept, so the
extremum sees every measurement of the trees it covers. A draft counted merges here too, on
the reasoning that more samples could only raise a derived cap — which is false for a
run-bounded window, because counting merges makes 20 runs span two days instead of three
weeks and the maximum is taken over LESS history, not more. See ADR-0068. ⚠️ THAT REJECTION
IS NARROWER THAN IT READS and #341 is where that was found: it argues about CALENDAR TIME,
which only bites while each BUILD is a sample. Twenty merges are twenty distinct trees.
Merges stay excluded because nothing has decided otherwise, which is a different sentence.
`configHash` is the score-affecting Stryker configuration these FLOORS were derived
under. Each CI run stamps its own; deploy compares them, and a mismatch refuses rather
than silently comparing two numbers that do not mean the same thing. Lowering
timeoutMS raises the score with no test touched, because a timeout counts as detected.
See scripts/lib/floors.ts for which options are hashed and which are not.
`fixtureHash` is the counting rule these CAPS were derived under: BOTH counting rules'
resolved options and BOTH inventory fixtures' expected totals, hashed in that order. An
ESLint upgrade that counts one more construct would raise every count with no branch
written — breaching every cap at once and reading as a regression nobody caused — so a
record counted under another rule is REFUSED rather than compared. ⚠️ THE THREE INSTALLED
VERSIONS ARE NOT INPUTS, since #341: a version string asserts nothing about behaviour, and
hashing them restarted every window on a bump that moved no number. An upgrade that really
counts differently reddens complexity.test.ts or cognitive.test.ts AT MERGE, and correcting
that fixture is what moves this stamp. See `fixtureHashOf` and ADR-0084.
⚠️ A SCORING-CONFIG CHANGE REFRESHES THE STAMP IN ITS OWN DIFF. `the-ratchet.md` §4's
route table already requires it — *change scoring config → `stryker.config.*` AND the
floors file's hash* — and it is written here too because this is the file the second
half of that diff lands in. FORGETTING IT IS NOT SILENT, AND UNTIL G56 IT WAS NOT CAUGHT
EITHER — the two are different sentences. `floorRefusals` reads a run stamped with a DIFFERENT
hash as evidence and refuses on it WHATEVER IS ARMED: the `armed` predicate guards only
the ABSENT-hash branch, so `unarmed` buys no quiet here and a forgotten stamp stops the
next `pnpm deploy:site` outright. IT IS ALSO CAUGHT EARLIER NOW: G56 (config-hash)
compares this stamp to `configHashOf(strykerConfig)` at MERGE, so a forgotten refresh
is a red pull request rather than a drift that reaches `main` green and ambushes
whoever next tries to publish. `pnpm mutation:stamp` writes the stamp; that command did
not exist while this hole did, and copying a hash by hand was the whole remedy. ⚠️ THE
GATE WATCHES `configHash` ONLY — `fixtureHash` below is watched by nothing at merge, and
that is still true while ITS ORIGINAL REASON IS NOT. ADR-0079 declined the gate because the
stamp pinned INSTALLED versions and a gate over one goes red on every Dependabot bump, which
a bot cannot re-derive. Since #341 the stamp holds BOTH counting rules' options and BOTH
inventory fixtures and no version at all, so that objection no longer describes it. Whether
it should now be watched is NOT DECIDED — see ADR-0084, which removed the premise and left
the refusal where it was. Meanwhile the genuinely silent half is the calibration window,
which reads 0 of 10 after any stamp move, because no run in the record carries the hash it
is counted against — a print, not a refusal, and indistinguishable from a window that has
simply not filled yet. ⚠️ IT IS NO LONGER 'FOREVER', and that is the whole of #341: a
dependency bump cannot move this stamp, so the window is restarted only by a counting change
somebody made. THE DEPLOY PRINT NOW NAMES
THE STAMP IT IS COUNTING UNDER beside that count, which separates a restarted window from
a young one for a reader who remembers the last one; it still cannot say WHY it moved,
which is #227. Refreshing an unarmed stamp
lowers nothing and costs no `notes` entry — there is no derived floor to re-derive.
Once a scope IS armed the same edit is a re-derivation and costs a justification like
any other lowering.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-08-23 BY #254, WHICH ADDED A SCOPE EXCLUSION. `stryker.config.mjs`
derives its `mutate` array from stryker.scopes.json, so excluding scripts/duplication-report.ts
changed the hashed configuration. NO FLOOR IS LOWERED AND NO `notes` ENTRY IS OWED: every floor
here is `unarmed`, so there is no derived floor to re-derive, which is exactly the case the
paragraph above describes. Recorded because the drift WAS AT THAT DATE caught by nothing — no
gate, no test and no CI check compared this stamp, so it reached `main` green and was found by
whoever next tried to publish. It was found here by reading a rendered record, not by a check.
That hole was #224, and G56 (config-hash) closed it: the same forgotten refresh is a red pull
request now. The sentence is kept as written because it is what was true on the day.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-08-26 BY #220, WHICH ADDED A SCOPE EXCLUSION. Same mechanism and same
cost as #254's refresh above: `stryker.config.mjs` derives `mutate` from stryker.scopes.json,
so excluding scripts/gh-post.ts changed the hashed configuration. NO FLOOR IS LOWERED AND NO
`notes` ENTRY IS OWED — every floor here is still `unarmed`. The calibration window reads 0 of
20 again from this commit, which is the silent half the paragraph above describes. THAT WAS
#224 WHEN THIS WAS WRITTEN and is now split: the stamp is compared at merge by G56, the deploy
print names the stamp it counts under, and WHY one moved is still #227's renovation marker.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-08-31 BY #292, WHICH BUMPED ESLINT 10.9.0 → 10.9.1. Unlike the two
refreshes above this was NOT a scope exclusion: `fixtureHash` hashes the exact eslint and
@typescript-eslint/parser versions AS INSTALLED, so a Dependabot bump moves the counting rule
with no configuration edited and no branch written. NO CAP IS LOWERED AND NO `notes` ENTRY IS
OWED — every cap here is `unarmed`, which is the case the paragraph above describes: refreshing
an unarmed stamp lowers nothing, and there is no derived cap to re-derive. ⚠️ THE COMPANION
BUMP #291 IS NOT THE CAUSE and was checked rather than assumed: it moved `@types/node` and
`puppeteer-core`, neither of which this hash reads. ⚠️ THE COST IS THE CALIBRATION WINDOW,
AGAIN — every complexity cap reads 0 of 20 from this commit, because no run in the record
carries the hash it is now counted against. That is the silent half, it was #224 when this was
written, and it is the third time this file has recorded it. ⚠️ G56 DOES NOT CLOSE THIS ONE:
it watches `configHash` and `fixtureHash` is deliberately left unwatched at merge, because a
gate over an INSTALLED version goes red on every Dependabot bump and a bot cannot re-derive a
stamp — declined in docs/adr/0079-the-floors-stamp-is-compared-at-merge.md, and whether a
detected change with no declared reason should itself refuse is #227's. ⚠️ IT BLOCKED A DEPLOY FOR TWO DAYS AND NOTHING SAID SO:
#292 reached `main` green on 2026-08-29 and the refusal was found on 2026-08-31 by somebody
trying to publish #313 — exactly the discovery path the paragraph above predicts, which is why
a dependency bump touching either tool should refresh this stamp in its own diff.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-09-08 BY #224, WHICH ADDED A SCOPE EXCLUSION — AND IS THE FIRST REFRESH A
CHECK ASKED FOR RATHER THAN A PERSON NOTICING. Same mechanism as #254's and #220's above:
`stryker.config.mjs` derives `mutate` from stryker.scopes.json, so excluding
scripts/stamp-floors.ts changed the hashed configuration. NO FLOOR IS LOWERED AND NO `notes`
ENTRY IS OWED — every floor here is still `unarmed`. ⚠️ WHAT IS DIFFERENT IS HOW IT WAS FOUND:
the exclusion landed in the same commit as G56, and G56 went red on it naming the new hash and
`pnpm mutation:stamp`. The three refreshes above were each found by a person reading a rendered
record, days late in two cases and two days into a blocked deploy in the third. ⚠️ THE COST IS
STILL THE CALIBRATION WINDOW — every mutation floor reads 0 of 20 from this commit — and the
deploy print now names the stamp it is counting under, so a reader can tell that restart from a
window that never filled.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-09-12 BY #337 AND #338 TOGETHER, WHICH MOVED BOTH HALVES OF THE RULE AT
ONCE — @typescript-eslint/parser 8.67.0 → 8.70.0 and eslint 10.9.1 → 10.10.0. This is #292's
mechanism exactly, one paragraph up, and the prediction it ends on: a dependency bump touching
either tool should refresh this stamp in its own diff, and NEITHER OF THOSE TWO DID. Both
reached `main` green, because `fixtureHash` is unwatched at merge by the deliberate choice
recorded above. NO CAP IS LOWERED AND NO `notes` ENTRY IS OWED — every cap here is `unarmed`,
so refreshing lowers nothing and there is no derived cap to re-derive. ⚠️ THE REFUSAL WAS REAL
AND WAS WATCHED ON PURPOSE, NOT INFERRED: `pnpm deploy:site --dry-run` on 1a18b70 printed
`FAILED: these caps were derived under a different counting rule`, naming floors
sha256:1026be16… against the run's sha256:a1e5752c…. ⚠️ THE COST IS THE CALIBRATION WINDOW,
AGAIN — it read 14 of 20 over 13 days before this commit and reads 0 of 20 after it, because no
run in the record carries the hash it is now counted against. FOURTH TIME. ⚠️ WHAT IS
DIFFERENT IS THAT IT WAS CAUGHT THE SAME DAY, inside the session that merged the two bumps,
rather than days later by somebody trying to publish — the discovery path is still a person
reading this file, which is #227's question and not closed by finding it early once.
⚠️ REFRESHED 2026-09-12 BY #341, AND THIS IS THE LAST VERSION-DRIVEN REFRESH BY CONSTRUCTION.
The four entries above are one failure repeated: `fixtureHash` digested the INSTALLED eslint,
parser and sonarjs versions, so every Dependabot bump restarted a window that nothing could
fill. Measured on #341: a stamp-moving release lands every 6.8 days and the window needed about
eighteen, so no cap was ever armed and none could be — three windows, best effort 14 of 20.
Measured the other way, the same tree under parser 8.67.0 with eslint 10.9.1 and under 8.70.0
with 10.10.0 returned ALL 64 ROWS IDENTICAL, with a planted one-row change proving the
comparison could see a difference. So the three version strings are gone from the digest and
the two INVENTORIES carry it instead: an upgrade that really counts differently reddens
complexity.test.ts or cognitive.test.ts at merge, and correcting that fixture is what moves
this stamp. ⚠️ WHAT IS LOST is an upgrade that changes counting on a construct no fixture
exercises — a real gap, bounded by how total the inventories are, and smaller than a window
that never fills. ⚠️ TWO MORE THINGS MOVED IN THE SAME DIFF, and both reach the FLOOR as well
as the cap because one `streakOf` walks both: the window is TEN and a sample is now ONE
DISTINCT TREE rather than one build. Measured: 24 nightlies across 23.2 days covered 13
distinct commits, so a run count overstated the evidence by 1.85 times and twenty runs never
meant twenty samples. The deploy print says `trees` for that reason. ⚠️ THE COST IS THE
CALIBRATION WINDOW ONE LAST TIME — every CAP reads 0 of 10 from this commit, because no run in
the record carries the new stamp. It fills in about 18 days and, unlike the four before it, no
dependency bump can restart it. ⚠️ THE FLOORS ARE A DIFFERENT CASE AND DO NOT READ ZERO: they
stamp on `configHash`, which this diff does not touch, so their streak survives and is merely
RECOUNTED IN TREES — observed falling from `14/20 runs` to `1/10 trees`, because four
consecutive nightlies had measured one commit. That is not a reset and not a regression; it is
what the record always held. See docs/adr/0084-the-counting-stamp-is-behaviour-not-a-version.md.
There is no override flag for any refusal this file produces, and that is the design
rather than an omission. See docs/adr/0061-the-mutation-floor-refuses-deploy.md and
docs/adr/0068-the-complexity-cap-only-falls.md.
